The [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Validate an XML sitemap — URL count, errors and a sample of entries. Enter your sitemap URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Fetch an XML sitemap and validate it: is it really a sitemap, how many URLs does it list, does every entry have a location, are the locations full URLs, and is it under the 50,000-URL limit for a single sitemap. A broken sitemap means search engines cannot find your pages — this tool finds the problem in seconds. The fetch runs from this site's server with the usual safety limits, and nothing is stored.

## How to use the Sitemap Checker

Start by typing or pasting your sitemap URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the full sitemap URL (usually yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml).
2. Run the check and read the URL count and any errors.
3. Fix the flagged problems and re-check.

## How it works

The [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

The fastest way to see what the [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What a valid sitemap needs

An XML file starting with an XML declaration, a <urlset> element, and one <url> entry per page, each with exactly one <loc> holding the page's full address. Optional <lastmod>, <changefreq> and <priority> elements are allowed but ignored by most search engines. A single sitemap holds at most 50,000 URLs and 50 MB — bigger sites split into several sitemaps listed in a sitemap index file.

## Common sitemap failures

The usual failures are: not XML at all (a 404 page served as the sitemap), entries without a <loc>, relative URLs instead of full ones, and URLs that no longer exist. A sitemap full of dead or redirected URLs wastes crawl budget and teaches search engines to trust the file less — keep it to live, indexable pages only.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Keep sitemaps to live, indexable pages only — no 404s or redirects.
- One sitemap holds at most 50,000 URLs — split bigger sites.
- List your sitemap in robots.txt so crawlers find it.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an XML sitemap?

An XML file listing a site's pages for search engines, so they can find and crawl them. Each entry has a <loc> with the page's full address. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many URLs can a sitemap hold?

At most 50,000 URLs and 50 MB per file. Bigger sites split into several sitemaps listed in a sitemap index. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What if my sitemap URL returns a 404?

Then there is no sitemap at that address — the tool says so. Check the address, and make sure your site actually generates one. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Should a sitemap include every page?

Every live, indexable page — but not 404s, redirects, admin pages or duplicates. A clean sitemap is trusted more than a big one. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sitemap Checker](/sitemap-checker) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
